common.detail_routed: This message would be sent to: {outputs}.
common.detail_deferred: {person} is not to be disturbed right now — {entities}. The message would be set aside, and delivered at {until}.
common.detail_presence: This alert does not notify everybody in every situation: its presence rule is {rule}, and {person} is currently {state}.
common.detail_silenced: {person} is not to be disturbed right now — {entities}. Only a critical alert would get through.
common.detail_silenced_temporary: {person} has been left in peace for a while, until {until}. Only a critical alert would get through.
common.detail_no_outputs: No device is listed for {person}, so there is nowhere to send this.
common.detail_not_in_audience: {person} is not one of the people {target} notifies.
common.detail_unknown_person: {target} wants to notify {person}, who is not in the list of people this house notifies.
common.detail_recursion: Every device listed for {person} points back at Notify Switchboard itself, so the message would go round in circles.
common.detail_expired: A message set aside for {person} would be given up: it has been set aside too long to still be worth delivering.
common.detail_not_notified: {person} heard nothing the last time {target} went off, so the back-to-normal message does not concern {person}.
common.detail_silenced_floor: {person} is not to be disturbed right now — {entities}, and only messages marked “{floor}” or above get through. A critical alert always does.
common.detail_unknown_target: “{target}” is no longer one of the messages this house knows how to send, so there is nowhere to deliver this one.
common.detail_delivery_failed: This message was handed to the devices listed for {person} and none of them took it, so it did not arrive.

user.title: Set up Notify Switchboard
user.description: Notify Switchboard decides who is told, on what, and when; your phones and your speakers are what ring — it never rings anything itself. Once it is installed, click Configure: add the people of the house and their devices first, then one alert per thing that can go wrong.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Notify Switchboard is already installed. One is all you need.

init.title: Notify Switchboard
init.description: Start with the people of the house: which devices each of them is told on, and when they are not to be disturbed. Then add one alert per thing that can go wrong — a water leak, a gate left open — choosing who should hear about it. Everything else is under Settings.

person.title: Add somebody
person.description: Pick who you want to add. The next screen already offers their phones and their Focus mode.

data_description.entity_id: Whether they are at home can be used to decide if they should be told.

edit_person.title: Change somebody
edit_person.description: Pick who you want to change. The next screen opens already filled in with what is saved.

person_outputs.title: Devices of {person}
person_outputs.description: Which devices does {person} get notifications on, and when should they not be disturbed?

data.night_schedule: Create a night schedule for this person

data_description.outputs: Their phones are already ticked. You can add a device that is not set up yet: it will be used as soon as it shows up.
data_description.silence_entities: A schedule, a switch, or the Focus mode of their iPhone: while it is on, their notifications are set aside.
data_description.night_schedule: Adds a schedule named after this person, from 10 pm to 7 am every day, to the quiet times above. It is yours afterwards: change its hours in Settings > Devices & services > Helpers.
data_description.advanced: Opens their wake time and morning summary next. Ticked, everything is saved when that screen is submitted.

person_advanced.title: The night of {person}
person_advanced.description: Optional. Without a time, the messages of the night arrive when the night schedule ends. A plain switch announces no end: with one of those, give a time, or the messages of the night are lost.

data.summary: Sum it all up in one message

data_description.wake_time: The time the night ends, for example 7:30. What was set aside during the night is delivered then. Empty: when the night schedule ends.
data_description.summary: One notification on waking, listing everything that was set aside, instead of one notification per message. On by default.

data_description.entity_id: Nothing is removed yet: the next screen says what this person will no longer hear about.

remove_person_confirm.title: Remove {person}?
remove_person_confirm.description:
{person} will no longer be told by: {targets}.

Their devices and their quiet times are forgotten by Notify Switchboard; the phones, schedules and switches themselves stay in Home Assistant.

data_description.confirm: Tick the box to confirm. To keep this person, close this window.

target.title: Add an alert
target.description: One thing that can go wrong in the house — a water leak, a gate left open — and the people to tell when it happens. These four answers are enough: importance, presence, buttons and wording all have a sensible value already.

data.name: Name
data.observer_mode: Tell people as soon as it goes off (recommended)

data_description.name: The name people see, for example Water leak. It is also the text sent when the alert supplies none.
data_description.alert_entity: A Home Assistant alert (alert.…). Home Assistant only lets you create those in YAML: if you have none, leave this empty — you will be shown what to do.
data_description.audience: The people concerned, and a speaker or a tablet if you want one. Nobody else hears anything.
data_description.observer_mode: On by default: Notify Switchboard watches what sets it off itself, so people are told at once, with nothing to copy and no restart.

target_edit.title: Changing {target}
target_edit.description: Change what “{target}” watches and who it tells. Its automation name does not change: {service}.

data.name: Name
data.observer_mode: Tell people as soon as it goes off (recommended)
data.escalation: Open what happens when the house is empty next

data_description.slug: The name to use in your automations. It was made from the first name of this alert and never changes, even if you rename it.
data_description.name: The name people see. It is also the text sent when the alert supplies none.
data_description.alert_entity: A Home Assistant alert (alert.…). Needed for the Acknowledge button. Empty: the alert only goes off when an automation calls it.
data_description.audience: The people concerned, and a speaker or a tablet if you want one. Nobody else hears anything.
data_description.observer_mode: Notify Switchboard watches what sets it off itself: people are told at once. This is the recommended way.
data_description.advanced: Importance, presence, buttons and wording. Ticked, everything is saved when the last screen is submitted.
data_description.escalation: Whether to raise the importance when nobody is home. Ticked, everything is saved when the last screen is submitted.

target_saved.title: Alert saved
target_saved.description:
You chose not to tell people as soon as it goes off, so the Home Assistant alert is what calls Notify Switchboard. Copy this block into your configuration once, replace binary_sensor.CHANGE_ME with the sensor to watch, then restart Home Assistant.

```yaml
{snippet}
```

To skip this step, change the alert and tick “Tell people as soon as it goes off” instead.

Everything else — importance, presence, buttons, wording — already has a sensible value. Tick the box below to set them up right away, or come back later through “Change an alert”.

data_description.advanced: Leave it unticked to save this alert as it is. Ticked, it is saved when the next screen is submitted.

target_ready.title: Alert saved
target_ready.description:
As soon as “{name}” goes off, these people are told: {audience}. There is nothing else to do.

Importance, presence, buttons and wording already have a sensible value. Tick the box below to set them up right away, or come back later through “Change an alert”.

data_description.advanced: Leave it unticked to save this alert as it is. Ticked, it is saved when the next screen is submitted.

target_ready_manual.title: Alert saved
target_ready_manual.description:
“{name}” is linked to no Home Assistant alert, so it will not go off on its own. Two ways to set it off:

1. In an automation, add the action {service} with a message.

2. Or create a Home Assistant alert by pasting this block into your configuration, then restart Home Assistant. Replace binary_sensor.CHANGE_ME with the sensor that reports the problem — the leak detector, the gate contact:

```yaml
{snippet}
```

Then change this alert and pick it under “What sets it off”.

data_description.advanced: Leave it unticked to save this alert as it is. Ticked, it is saved when the next screen is submitted.

target_advanced.title: Advanced settings of {target}
target_advanced.description: Everything about {target} that already has a sensible value. Nothing here is required, and what you leave alone keeps the value it has.

data.default_data: Technical settings added to every message

data_description.default_priority: Only a critical alert gets through when somebody is not to be disturbed or has put the alert on hold.
data_description.presence_rule: Does somebody have to be at home, to be out, or does it not matter, to be told?
data_description.allow_acknowledge: Adds a button to the notification that turns the alert off.
data_description.snooze_minutes: Durations in minutes, comma separated, for example 15, 60. Empty: no "later" button at all.
data_description.default_data: If the message already says the same thing, the message wins.
data_description.message: Optional, and used only when people are told as soon as it goes off. Empty: the name of the alert is sent. Advanced users can write a template.
data_description.done_message: Optional, sent when the Home Assistant alert turns off, if people are told as soon as it goes off. Empty: a ready-made text is sent.
data_description.default_title: Title used when the call gives none, and for every message Notify Switchboard sends on its own.
data_description.clear_done: Take the back-to-normal notification off the phones that received it, once the alert is over. Off by default: it rings, then it stays.

target_escalation.title: What happens when the house is empty
target_escalation.description: What {target} does when nobody it tells is at home. Nothing else about it is touched. This choice only matters when the alert also tells people who are out: if it only tells people who are in, an empty house means nobody is told at all, and there is nothing left to raise.

data.escalate_when_nobody_home: Raise the importance when the house is empty

data_description.escalate_when_nobody_home: One step louder, for that message only: not very important becomes normal, normal becomes important, important becomes critical. An alert that is already critical does not move, and presence still decides who is told.

edit_target.title: Change an alert
edit_target.description: Pick the alert to change. The next screen opens already filled in with what is saved, and leads to its advanced settings.

data_description.slug: Nothing is removed yet: the next screen says who will no longer be told.

remove_target_confirm.title: Remove {target}?
remove_target_confirm.description:
Nobody will be told about {target} any more: {persons}.

Whatever still calls {service} — a Home Assistant alert, an automation, a card — will reach nobody.

data_description.confirm: Tick the box to confirm. To keep this alert, close this window.

general.title: Settings
general.description: What concerns the whole house rather than one person or one alert, and the two test messages.

menu_options.critical_payload: Make phones ring for critical alerts
menu_options.ttl: How long a message set aside stays useful
menu_options.test_target: Send a test message through an alert

default_target.title: Alert used by default
default_target.description: The alert used when something asks Notify Switchboard to tell people without saying which alert it is about.

data_description.default_target: Used when nothing else is said.

critical_payload.title: Make phones ring for critical alerts
critical_payload.description: A critical alert is the only one that gets through when somebody is not to be disturbed. With this on, it also rings their phone.

data.critical_payload: Make phones ring for critical alerts

data_description.critical_payload: A critical alert then rings the phone even when it is set to Do Not Disturb. On by default; it only concerns the Home Assistant app.

ttl.title: How long a message set aside stays useful
ttl.description: A message set aside while somebody was not to be disturbed is not necessarily worth delivering twelve hours later. Say, per importance, how long it is still worth delivering. An empty field means it never expires. Critical alerts are never set aside, so they have no delay here.

data_description.info: In minutes, counted from the moment the message was set aside.
data_description.normal: In minutes, counted from the moment the message was set aside.
data_description.high: In minutes, counted from the moment the message was set aside. Empty by default: these messages never expire.

test_target.title: Send a test message through an alert
test_target.description: Sends one real test message, to everybody this alert tells.

data_description.slug: The alert to try. The message counts like any other.

test_person.title: Send somebody a test message
test_person.description: Sends one real test message to this person, through an alert that tells them.

data_description.entity_id: The alert used by default is used when it tells this person, otherwise the first alert that tells them.

test_result.title: Test result

error.not_a_person: Pick somebody from the people of the house.
error.recursive_output: A device cannot point back at Notify Switchboard itself.
error.component_service_output: This is not a device: pick a phone, a speaker or a tablet.
error.invalid_output: This name holds characters that are not allowed.
error.invalid_entity: This does not exist (any more) in your home.
error.invalid_slug: Lowercase letters, digits and the _ sign only.
error.duplicate_slug: Another alert already goes by this name.
error.invalid_priority: Pick one of: not very important, normal, important, critical.
error.invalid_presence_rule: Pick one of: always, at home or out; only people who are at home; only people who are out.
error.unknown_person: This alert wants to tell somebody who is not in the list of people this house notifies.
error.invalid_snooze_minutes: Use whole, positive minutes, comma separated.
error.invalid_default_data: This field is for technical settings; leave it empty if you are not sure.
error.not_confirmed: Tick the box to confirm, or close this window to cancel.
error.night_schedule_failed: The night schedule could not be created. Create a schedule in Settings > Devices & services > Helpers, then pick it above.

abort.nothing_to_remove: There is nothing to remove yet.
abort.nothing_to_edit: There is nothing to edit yet.
abort.nothing_to_test: No alert tells this person anything, so there is nothing to send them. Add them to an alert first.

unknown_target.title: An alert that was asked for does not exist
unknown_target.description: Something asked for the alert “{slug}”, which does not exist. The message was given up. Create that alert, or fix whatever asks for it.

missing_output.title: A device no longer answers
missing_output.description: The device “{output}” has received nothing several times in succession: it does not exist, or every send ended in an error. The messages meant for it are lost. Repair it, or take it out of the person's devices.

invalid_service_target.title: Something keeps asking for an alert that does not exist
invalid_service_target.description: Notify Switchboard cannot find the alert “{value}”. Something — most often a card or a script left on a renamed alert — keeps asking for it. Fix it, or create that alert.

invalid_service_person.title: Something keeps naming somebody it cannot tell
invalid_service_person.description: Notify Switchboard cannot find “{value}”: that person is not in the list of people of the house, or is not told by this alert. Fix whatever asks for them, or add that person.

invalid_service_calls_many.title: Something keeps asking with names that do not exist
invalid_service_calls_many.description: Notify Switchboard has now refused more than {count} different alerts or people. Rather than one warning per name, this one stands for them all. Something is making up names that do not exist — most often an automation producing a wrong name. Fix it; this warning goes away when you restart Notify Switchboard.

person_without_user_id.title: Somebody is not linked to a Home Assistant account
person_without_user_id.description: {person} gets notifications with the Acknowledge and Later buttons, but their card is not linked to any Home Assistant account. Notify Switchboard therefore cannot tell who pressed, and applies the action to everybody the alert tells. Link this person to their account in Settings > People, then reload Notify Switchboard.

person_without_outputs.title: Somebody has no device at all
person_without_outputs.description: At least one alert tells {person}, but no device is listed for {person}: every message meant for them is lost. Open the Notify Switchboard options, edit that person and give them at least one device.

alert_entity_missing.title: What sets an alert off no longer exists
alert_entity_missing.description: The alert “{slug}” is linked to a Home Assistant alert that no longer exists ({entity_id}). So it never goes off on its own, and its Acknowledge button turns nothing off. Create that Home Assistant alert again, or empty the alert's “What sets it off” field, then reload Notify Switchboard.

acknowledge_not_allowed.message: The alert {target} has no Acknowledge button: it is linked to no Home Assistant alert, or the button is turned off for it.

snooze_minutes_not_offered.message: The alert {target} does not offer a {minutes} min hold. It offers: {offered}.

unknown_person.message: {person} is not in the list of people Notify Switchboard knows about.

person_not_in_audience.message: {person} is not one of the people the alert {target} tells.

invalid_silence_minutes.message: Peace and quiet lasts between {min} and {max} minutes; {minutes} is neither.

no_loaded_entry.message: Notify Switchboard is switched off, so it can do nothing. Switch it back on, then try again.

options.critical: Critical — gets through even when somebody is not to be disturbed

options.home_only: Only people who are at home

acknowledge.name: Acknowledge
acknowledge.description: Turns off the Home Assistant alert linked to an alert, exactly as the Acknowledge button of a notification does.

target.name: Alert
target.description: The alert concerned (its automation name). It must be linked to a Home Assistant alert and offer the Acknowledge button.

snooze.name: Put on hold
snooze.description: Stops the messages of one alert for a while, for one person or for everybody that alert tells.

target.name: Alert
target.description: The alert concerned (its automation name), the one to put on hold.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: For how long. It has to be one of the durations the alert offers.

person.name: Person
person.description: For whom. Leave empty for everybody that alert tells.

unsnooze.name: Take off hold
unsnooze.description: Starts the messages again straight away, without waiting for the hold to run out.

target.name: Alert
target.description: The alert concerned (its automation name), the one to start again.

person.name: Person
person.description: For whom. Leave empty for everybody that alert tells.

silence.name: Do not disturb somebody
silence.description: Stops disturbing somebody for a while, for every alert. Their own schedules and switches are left untouched; only a critical alert still gets through.

person.name: Person
person.description: Who is not to be disturbed. They have to be in the list of people this house notifies.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: For how long: from 1 minute to 1440 (a day).

unsilence.name: Make somebody reachable again
unsilence.description: Cancels straight away a do-not-disturb set by the action above. Does nothing when the person was not left in peace that way.

explain.name: Explain
explain.description: Answers the question “what would happen to a message sent right now to this alert?”, person by person, without sending anything. Call it asking for the answer.

target.name: Alert
target.description: The alert concerned (its automation name), the one to look at.

priority.name: Importance
priority.description: The importance to assume. Leave empty for the one the alert uses by default, exactly as a real message does.

person.name: Person
person.description: Whom to answer about. Leave empty for everybody that alert tells.
